subject: DPA: Privacy annex for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — subprocessor & key controls
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@skylenshealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@skylenshealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T08:15:00+02:00
Subject: DPA: Privacy annex for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — subprocessor & key controls

Hi Mateo / Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team has a few specific asks as part of the DPA addendum for Private Deployment (VPC / on-prem):

- Clear statement of customer-controlled keys (BYOK) and whether Redwood ever has access to unencrypted data or plaintext model inputs when BYOK is enabled.
- Subprocessor list for Private (including operator or managed-service subprocessors) and a mechanism for pre-notification of new subprocessors.
- Expected cross-border transfer posture for logs/telemetry and any metadata retained by Redwood in the EU deployment.
- Break-glass / escrow scenarios and the controls around emergency operator access (who, for how long, and how audited).

I've attached a short list of questions (Skylens-privacy-questions.docx). Can you propose language or a small annex we can circulate to legal? We need a draft by early next week if possible.

Sara
Legal Counsel, Skylens Health

Attachment: Skylens-privacy-questions.docx (docx, 18KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@skylenshealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:48:00+02:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Privacy annex for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — subprocessor & key controls

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Attached is an initial draft annex that attempts to address each bullet; quick highlights below and inline answers to the attachment.

Key points (summary):
- BYOK: When a customer elects BYOK, customer keys are used to encrypt persistent storage and backups at rest. Redwood does not retain plaintext of model inputs or decrypted outputs in persistent storage. Runtime inference requires keys be provisioned to the local keystore (customer-managed KMS).
- Operator access: We commit to operator separation via role-based access controls; emergency access is strictly limited and requires an explicit break-glass process (approval from two SRE leads + marketplace of audit traces).
- Subprocessors: For Private deployments we split subprocessors into (a) infrastructure partners (hosted vendors) and (b) operator services (on-call rotations, monitoring). We can provide a current list and 30-day notice for additions.
- Cross-border transfers: For EU-region VPCs, logs and telemetry remain in-region by default; any necessary international transfers will be listed and require either SCCs or customer consent depending on jurisdiction.

I included inline comments in the PDF (RDW-privdep-privacy-annex-draft_v1.pdf). If that looks good we can convert to a DPA addendum and point your legal team to the Drive link for edits.

Propose a 30-minute sync on Thursday to run through outstanding points — Kim, Priya: available?

— Mateo
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW-privdep-privacy-annex-draft_v1.pdf (pdf, 42KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@skylenshealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T10:12:00+02:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Privacy annex for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — subprocessor & key controls

Thanks, Mateo — attaching a couple of suggested edits. A few items I want to flag for Skylens legal before the call:

1) Subprocessor granularity: We'll provide a named list for current subprocessors and a category-based notice (e.g., monitoring provider, on-call operator) for future additions. If Skylens needs pre-approval rather than notice, we can discuss a mutually-agreed approval workflow (takes longer to operationalize).

2) BYOK scope: Clarify that BYOK covers persistent stores and backups, but there is ephemeral memory during inference that is not persisted. We propose a retention minimization clause and mandatory in-memory shredding on inference completion.

3) Escrow/break-glass: We can offer an optional escrow for key recovery under legal process + two-person approval, with a full audit trail (immutable logs) and automatic customer notification. This should be an add-on in procurement (not standard).

4) Evidence: Skylens asked for SOC2/ISO artifacts — we'll produce redacted evidence and a scoped SOC2 extract for the Private deployment (controls mapping).

Inline comments in the PDF point to specific paragraph edits.

Kim
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
From: Legal Ops <legal-ops@skylenshealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T11:05:00+02:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Privacy annex for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — subprocessor & key controls

Hi Mateo / Kim,

Thanks for the rapid draft. A few follow-ups from our side before the call:

- Break-glass / escrow: We need explicit maximum hold time (for example: any emergency key recovery window must be <= 72 hours and we need to define scope of permitted operations during that window).
- Auditability: The annex should enumerate the logging artifacts you will provide (who accessed what, timestamps, reason codes) and the retention period for those logs.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable for category changes; for new named subprocessors handling customer data we require 14 days pre-notification and the option to object (standard DPA process).
- Cross-border telemetry: If any PII-derived metadata leaves EU region for processing or vendor support, we need SCCs in place; please confirm current list of destinations.

If you can add those bullets into the draft prior to our meeting, we'll circulate to our CTO and procurement. Meeting invite to follow.

Thanks,
Skylens Legal Ops
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Legal Ops <legal-ops@skylenshealth.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@skylenshealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T09:32:00+02:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Privacy annex for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — subprocessor & key controls

Appreciate the detail — we've incorporated the requested bullets into the second draft on Drive (link below). Quick responses inline here: 

- Emergency window: We can commit to a maximum 72-hour temporary access window for break-glass with two authorized approvers and automatic customer notification.
- Logging artifacts: We will provide access logs with principal identity, timestamp, and reason code. Retention for audit logs is 12 months by default, extendable contractually.
- Subprocessor notice: Agree to 14-day pre-notification for any new named subprocessor that will handle customer data; objection window and escalation path will be documented.
- SCCs: Current external support destinations for Skylens EU region are Norway (support partner), UK (field engineer access), and US for limited escalation. We will list these and commit to SCCs or equivalent safeguards; details in the draft.

Drive draft: https://drive.google.com/rdw/privdep-dpa-draft
Docusign (once ready): https://app.docusign.com/rooms/rdw-dpa-addendum-7834

Next steps: 1) I suggest Skylens legal review the Drive draft and collect comments; 2) we take 30-min call to align on final edits; 3) we circulate a redline for procurement to confirm pricing for escrow add-on.

— Mateo
